items.source: frozen per-item lane banks, dataset csoai/gspc-peritem-rows-2026-08-12 (the same files ci/frontier-runner.py reads)
items.selection_rule: sort the lane's (item, gold) pairs by sha256(lane + NUL + item_text) ascending, take the first items_per_lane
items.grader: harness/gspc-top100/mill_hub_queue.py::read_label; an answer that is not one menu label is the category UNPARSED, which counts as its own category
items.item_visibility: PUBLIC_BANK (the held-out question is open, see HELDOUT-DESIGN.md)

call_rules.order: all (item, repeat) calls of one batch shuffled together with a seeded RNG, so time of day is spread across items

declared_sampling.seed: unset unless the provider requires one

call_rules.system_prompt: none (calibration condition C3 changes it on purpose)

statistic.name: mean_tv_permutation
statistic.definition: for item i let p_i and q_i be the share of each answer category in the baseline batch and the new batch; TV_i = 0.5 * sum_c |p_ic - q_ic|; T = mean over items of TV_i
statistic.null: within each item, pool the 2K answers and re-split them at random into K and K; recompute T
statistic.p_value: (1 + number of permuted T >= observed T) / (1 + b)
statistic.rng_seed_rule: integer from sha256(protocol_id + comparison_id), so a comparison can be recomputed byte for byte

flag_rule.meaning: the answer distribution on the probe items moved against the baseline by more than the model's own run-to-run spread. It says THAT behaviour moved on these items. It does not say why, where, or whether it matters.

baseline.first_run_for_a_model: writes the baseline (K repeats), compares nothing, state BASELINE_SET
baseline.replacement: never automatic; only by a person starting the workflow with rebaseline=true, which records the hash of the baseline it replaces
baseline.signed: digest record signed in GitHub Actions only

calibration.model_family: one open model, size chosen so the run fits free compute; exact repo, revision and file hashes are written to calibration-pins.json and committed BEFORE any calibration run

C1.name: different revision of the same model

C2.name: quantised copy of the same revision

C3.name: changed system prompt (one added neutral sentence, text fixed in calibration-pins.json)

calibration.trial: one full batch (all items x K repeats) under the condition, compared to the one baseline batch with the unchanged statistic and flag rule
calibration.reported: for each condition: flags / trials with an exact 95% (Wilson) interval, plus mean T. C0 is the false-flag rate; C1 to C4 are the detection rates. Every condition is reported, including those that go badly.
calibration.synthetic_checks: unit tests with planted and unplanted synthetic data prove the code, not the method. They are never reported as calibration.

enable_conditions: a named person has confirmed, per provider, that the governing agreement permits benchmarking and publishing the result; recorded in scripts/silent-change/paid_models.json as confirmed_by_person and confirmed_on
C0 false-flag rate has been measured and published beside the watch
watch.schedule: one batch per model per day at a random minute inside a fixed window
watch.publication: a flag is printed with the calibration rates beside it. It is never labelled a cause, a degradation, or a safety verdict. Own-council models are never ranked publicly; the watch has no ranking at all.
watch.multiplicity: no correction across models, banks and days is applied. The expected number of false flags per day is models x C0 rate and is stated beside every report.

not_done_by_this_protocol: weights, raw reasoning and training data of paid models (stay in unmeasured[])
any claim about items outside the probe items
any comparison of one model with another

addendum_1.data_quality_gate: if more than 5 percent of the calls of a batch fail at the transport (network error, timeout, HTTP error other than a refusal of credentials), the batch is UNCHECKABLE: it is not compared, not counted as a flag and not counted in any rate. A failed fetch is never read as 'unchanged' or 'changed'. UNPARSED answers are not transport failures; they stay a category.

addendum_2.scope: calibration run on free GitHub-hosted runners; sections 1 to 6 and the statistic, the flag rule and addendum_1 are unchanged

open_model.family: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct GGUF (Apache-2.0), served by llama.cpp release b12651 llama-server on the runner
open_model.server: one serial request at a time, prompt cache off (cache_prompt false), context 2048, a fixed server seed per shard, the model's own chat template; no other sampling setting is changed

BASE.role: the one baseline batch for C0 to C4

C1.change: a sibling model (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, same Q8_0 quantisation). Replaces 'a different revision of the same model': the 0.5B GGUF files have the same sha256 in every revision of their repository (checked 23 Nov for the first and the second commit), so no different revision exists to run.

C2.change: the same weights quantised Q4_K_M instead of Q8_0

C3.system: Read the question carefully before answering.

BASE5.role: the one baseline batch for C5

C5.change: none: the no-change control while the model is sampling, compared with BASE5

addendum_2.why_c5: At temperature 0 on a serial local server the same file is expected to repeat its answers, so C0 may show exactly no movement and then says little about false flags under run-to-run noise. C5 is the same no-change test while answers vary. It is a second false-flag rate, reported beside C0. It was added before any data and is never dropped if it goes badly.
addendum_2.sharding: batches are grouped by model file and cut into jobs of equal size. The size comes from a seconds-per-batch planning constant in calibration-pins.json; it changes which job runs a batch, never what a batch is, so it is not a method parameter. Every comparison is against the one baseline batch of its own kind.
addendum_2.completeness: the combined report is signed only if every registered batch is present. A missing or UNCHECKABLE batch is reported as such and counted out of the denominator of its condition; a report with a missing batch is not signed.
addendum_2.rates: for each of C0 to C5: flags / comparable trials, exact Wilson 95% interval, mean T, as in section 7. Reading aids: with 0 flags in 30 trials the upper bound is about 0.11 and with 0 in 20 about 0.16; 10 of 10 flags give a lower bound of about 0.72.
addendum_2.second_view: an illustrative CUSUM and Shewhart view of the per-trial T series (measurement/experiments/metrology-controls/check_standard.py). Its reference and spread come from resampling the baseline batch alone, its time axis is the trial order, and it carries no false-alarm rate. It never changes a flag, a rate or the signed payload.
addendum_2.rehearsal: a local run on 2 items and 3 repeats proves the pipeline. Its rows are never published, never signed and never counted; the report refuses any batch marked rehearsal.

runner_limits.source: docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits (the github/docs source file, read 23 Nov 2026); the plan of this repository is unverified, so the matrix runs at most 8 jobs at once
